metas.name: The Straight Story
metas.description:
Captures sincerity with zero irony. An old man who cannot drive a car rides a lawnmower tractor across two states to see his estranged, dying brother — David Lynch's gentlest film.

Alvin Straight, a 73-year-old, learns that his estranged brother, Lyle is critically ill. Unable to drive, Alvin embarks on a journey from Iowa to Mt. Zion by riding a lawn mower.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description:
Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

An Israeli film director interviews fellow veterans of the 1982 invasion of Lebanon to reconstruct his own memories of his term of service in that conflict.

metas.name: Flee
metas.description:
Captures telling a hidden life story for the first time. An animated documentary about a refugee from Afghanistan settled in Denmark, recounting flight, family separation and a secret he has kept from everyone.

A man looks back over his life as he grapples with a painful secret he has kept hidden for 20 years, one that threatens to derail the life he has built for himself and his soon to be husband.

metas.name: The Social Network
metas.description:
Captures a creation myth told as a betrayal. Facebook's founding at pure dialogue velocity — dorm rooms, depositions, and a friendship converted into equity.

As Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg creates the social networking site that would become known as Facebook, he is sued by the twins who claimed he stole their idea and by the co-founder who was later squeezed out of the business.

metas.name: Lawrence of Arabia
metas.description:
Captures a man inventing himself at desert scale. Nearly four hours: the landscape is a character, and so is the gap between the legend being built and the person inside it.

The story of T.E. Lawrence, the English officer who successfully united and led the diverse, often warring, Arab tribes during World War I in order to fight the Turks.

metas.name: Dog Day Afternoon
metas.description:
Captures a bank robbery becoming a live street spectacle. One hot Brooklyn afternoon, Pacino working the crowd outside like a rally, and the reason for the robbery arriving piece by piece.

Three amateur robbers plan to hold up a Brooklyn bank. A nice, simple robbery: Walk in, take the money, and run. Unfortunately, the supposedly uncomplicated heist suddenly becomes a bizarre nightmare as everything that could go wr...

metas.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
metas.description:
Captures celebrity worship in 1882. A famous outlaw ageing and paranoid, and a young admirer who memorised his life from dime novels and moves into his orbit — slow, golden, narrated like a history book.

Robert Ford, who has idolized Jesse James since childhood, tries hard to join the resurgent gang of the Missouri outlaw, but gradually becomes resentful of the bandit leader.

metas.name: First Man
metas.description:
Captures the Moon landing from inside a grieving, taciturn man. Armstrong as an engineer who can land anything except in his own family's pain; the flights are rattling, cramped and procedural.

A look back at the life of astronaut Neil Armstrong and the legendary space mission that led him to become the first man to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

metas.name: Senna
metas.description:
Captures speed, faith and charisma, entirely from archive. Ayrton Senna's career built only from period footage and voices — rivalry with Prost, Brazil on his helmet, in-car laps that feel like prayer at 300 km/h.

A documentary on Brazilian Formula One racing driver Ayrton Senna, who won the F1 world championship three times before his death at age 34.

metas.name: Raging Bull
metas.description:
Captures self-destruction in a family kitchen as much as a ring. Jake LaMotta's jealousy and violence at home filmed with the same intensity as the fights; he can take any punch except accountability.

The life of boxer Jake LaMotta, whose violence and temper that led him to the top in the ring destroyed his life outside of it.

metas.name: All the President's Men
metas.description:
Captures journalism as shoe leather. Watergate as phone calls, parking garages, notebooks and editors asking 'what else do you have?' — verification repeated until a presidency moves.

"The Washington Post" reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein uncover the details of the Watergate scandal that leads to President Richard Nixon's resignation.

metas.name: Spotlight
metas.description:
Captures an investigation as a team slowly realising the size of the room they're in. Boston Globe reporters, church abuse, sealed records, survivors telling it plainly — no heroics beyond persistence.

The true story of how the Boston Globe uncovered the massive scandal of child molestation and cover-up within the local Catholic Archdiocese, shaking the entire Catholic Church to its core.

metas.name: The Insider
metas.description:
Captures the cost of telling the truth inside two corporations at once. A tobacco scientist bound by confidentiality, a TV producer with a network to protect, and an interview everyone with money wants buried.

A research chemist comes under personal and professional attack when he decides to appear in a 60 Minutes exposé on Big Tobacco.

metas.name: Close-Up
metas.description:
Captures a poor film fan who wanted, briefly, to be the man whose name he borrowed. In Tehran a man impersonates a famous director to a family, is arrested, and then everyone involved re-enacts their own case, including the trial.

The true story of Hossain Sabzian, a cinephile who impersonated the director Mohsen Makhmalbaf to convince a family they would star in his so-called new film.

metas.name: The Colour of Pomegranates
metas.description:
Captures a poet's life as a series of icons instead of events. An Armenian troubadour rendered in tableaux — books, blood, grapes, lace — with almost no dialogue and no interest in explaining itself.

The life of the Armenian poet Sayat-Nova, from childhood to death: his spiritual journey, artistic endeavors, and inner conflicts within the cultural and historical context of Armenia. Hailed as revolutionary by Mikhail Vartanov.

metas.name: The Favourite
metas.description:
Captures court power as intimate warfare. Two women compete to be Queen Anne's favourite — her bed, her ear, her rabbits — through fisheye candlelit corridors, with a lonely, raging queen at the centre.

In early 18th-century England, the status quo at the court is upset when a new servant arrives and endears herself to a frail Queen Anne.

metas.name: Crumb
metas.description:
Captures how the same upbringing produces a famous artist, a broken man, and something in between. Cartoonist R. Crumb and his two brothers, all shaped by one brutal household, in Terry Zwigoff's unsparing family portrait.

An intimate portrait of controversial cartoonist Robert Crumb and his traumatized family.

metas.name: Capturing the Friedmans
metas.description:
Captures a family performing normality for a camera while everything underneath it collapses. A family accused of horrific crimes, told largely through their own compulsive home videos, which keep contradicting the legal case and each other.

Follows the Friedmans, a seemingly typical, upper-middle-class Jewish family whose world is instantly transformed when the father and his youngest son are arrested and charged with shocking and horrible crimes.

metas.name: The Fog of War
metas.description:
Captures a brilliant man half-confessing to catastrophe. Robert McNamara, architect of Vietnam escalation, now in his eighties, lays out eleven lessons from his life in power — you decide whether the other half is honesty or self-defence.

The story of America as seen through the eyes of the former Secretary of Defense under President John F. Kennedy and President Lyndon B. Johnson, Robert McNamara.

metas.name: Grizzly Man
metas.description:
Captures a man narrating himself into a story nature never agreed to be part of. Herzog assembles Timothy Treadwell's own footage: thirteen summers living among Alaskan bears he insisted loved him, before one of them killed him.

A devastating and heart-rending take on grizzly bear activists Timothy Treadwell and Amie Huguenard, who were killed in October of 2003 while living among grizzly bears in Alaska.

metas.name: Dear Zachary: A Letter to a Son About His Father
metas.description:
Captures grief and legal-system failure like nothing else here. It begins as a film for a baby about the father he'll never meet, murdered before he was born — then the case takes a turn mid-production that is almost unbearable.

A filmmaker decides to memorialize a murdered friend when his friend's ex-girlfriend announces she is expecting his son.

metas.name: Man on Wire
metas.description:
Captures pure, pointless, joyful daring — a crime with no victim and no motive except beauty. Philippe Petit's 1974 tightrope walk between the Twin Towers, told like a heist film by the crew who smuggled the rigging up.

A look at tightrope walker Philippe Petit's daring, but illegal, high-wire routine performed between New York City's World Trade Center's twin towers in 1974, what some consider, "the artistic crime of the century".

metas.name: The Imposter
metas.description:
Captures how badly people want a story to be true. A missing Texas teenager 'returns' three years later, older and with a French accent — and his family accepts him. The man himself explains exactly how he did it.

A documentary centered on a young man in Spain who claims to a grieving Texas family that he is their 16-year-old son who has been missing for 3 years.

metas.name: Citizenfour
metas.description:
Captures history happening at the speed of a man checking over his shoulder. Laura Poitras was already filming when Edward Snowden contacted her, so the leak of the century unfolds in a Hong Kong hotel room in real time.

A documentarian and a reporter travel to Hong Kong for the first of many meetings with Edward Snowden.

metas.name: Amy
metas.description:
Captures the machinery of fame eating a person whose talent is right there on screen the whole time. Amy Winehouse's rise and destruction assembled from home video, voicemails and the tabloid footage that hunted her.

Archival footage and personal testimonials present an intimate portrait of the life and career of British singer/songwriter Amy Winehouse.

metas.name: O.J.: Made in America
metas.description:
Captures a whole country's contradictions in one man's story. Nearly eight hours, and not really about a murder trial: Los Angeles, race, celebrity and policing across fifty years, with Simpson as the thread running through all of it.

A chronicle of the rise and fall of O.J. Simpson, whose high-profile murder trial exposed the extent of American racial tensions, revealing a fractured and divided nation.

metas.name: For Sama
metas.description:
Captures war from inside a family instead of inside a news report. Waad Al-Kateab films five years of the siege of Aleppo as a letter to her baby daughter, explaining why they stayed.

An intimate and epic journey into a young woman's experience of war during the revolution in Aleppo, Syria.

metas.name: Dick Johnson Is Dead
metas.description:
Captures dying approached with slapstick, tenderness and total honesty at once. Kirsten Johnson stages elaborate fake deaths for her psychiatrist father, who has dementia, so the two of them can rehearse losing each other.

A daughter helps her father prepare for the end of his life.

metas.name: Fire of Love
metas.description:
Captures a love story where the third party is the Earth itself. Volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft filmed each other at the edge of eruptions for twenty years, knowing the work would probably kill them. It did, together, in 1991.

Intrepid scientists and lovers Katia and Maurice Krafft died in a volcanic explosion doing the very thing that brought them together: unraveling the mysteries of volcanoes by capturing the most explosive imagery ever recorded.

metas.name: The Emperor's Naked Army Marches On
metas.description:
Captures one man's war that never ended: veteran Kenzo Okuzaki tours Japan forcing his former officers to answer on camera for executions and cannibalism in New Guinea, while director Kazuo Hara's crew effectively enlists in his campaign.

Kenzo Okuzaki, a 62-year-old anarchist veteran of the New Guinea campaign in World War II, sets out to conduct interviews with survivors and relatives to find the truth behind atrocities committed by Japanese military, in particular the unexplained killing of two Japanese privates in his unit.

metas.name: Extreme Private Eros: Love Song 1974
metas.description:
Captures a filmmaker turning his merciless method on himself: Hara follows his ex-wife, radical feminist Miyuki Takeda, through lovers, communes and an unassisted birth, while his new partner records the sound — intimacy documented past every comfortable limit.

In this uncomfortably intimate film, documentary filmmaker Kazuo Hara visits his ex-girlfriend Miyuki and records her new relationships.

metas.name: The Look of Silence
metas.description:
Captures confrontation inverted: Adi, whose brother was murdered in Indonesia's 1965 purges, visits the killers under cover of eye exams and asks about the killings to their faces — no shouting, only unbearable quiet where they still hold power.

A family that survived the genocide in Indonesia confronts the men who killed one of their brothers.

metas.name: Portrait of Jason
metas.description:
Captures the point where performance stops protecting a man: hustler and would-be cabaret act Jason Holliday performs his life all night for Shirley Clarke's provoking camera, until the act slowly, visibly cracks.

Black gay prostitute Jason Holliday is rigorously interviewed on his story and character, revealing nuanced truths about life and art.

metas.name: Cameraperson
metas.description:
Captures a career of looking, reckoned with: Kirsten Johnson cuts decades of outtakes from other people's difficult documentaries — Bosnia, Darfur, her own mother's decline — into a memoir about what pointing a camera at someone's worst day costs.

Exposing her role behind the camera, Kirsten Johnson reaches into the vast trove of footage she has shot over decades around the world. What emerges is a visually bold memoir and a revelatory interrogation of the power of the camera.

metas.name: Chasing Ice
metas.description:
Captures climate change made visible at human time-scale, no argument required. Time-lapse cameras planted on glaciers play back years of retreat in seconds — including a calving event the size of a city district, caught by chance.

Follow National Geographic photographer James Balog across the Arctic as he deploys time-lapse cameras designed for one purpose: to capture a multi-year record of the world's changing glaciers.

metas.name: The Salt of the Earth
metas.description:
Captures what a lifetime of looking at suffering does to a person, and one answer to it. Photographer Sebastião Salgado walks through forty years of famine, war and exodus in his own images, then turns to restoring a dead forest — and it works.

The life and work of photographer Sebastião Salgado, who has spent forty years documenting societies in hidden corners of the world.

metas.name: Searching for Sugar Man
metas.description:
Captures fame existing in full, in a place the famous person never knew about. Detroit singer Rodriguez, a flop at home in the 1970s and rumoured dead, was bigger than Elvis in apartheid South Africa. The most joyful film in its batch.

Two South Africans set out to discover what happened to their unlikely musical hero, the mysterious 1970s rock n roller, Rodriguez.

metas.name: Anvil! The Story of Anvil
metas.description:
Captures artistic persistence with no payoff in sight. Toronto's own Anvil: fifty-something metal pioneers who nearly made it in 1982, now delivering school lunches and playing to five people in Prague, still completely serious about the band.

Since 1978, Anvil has become one of heavy metal's most influential yet commercially unsuccessful acts. In 2006, after a fledging European tour Anvil sets out to record their thirteenth album and continue to follow their dreams.

metas.name: Won't You Be My Neighbor?
metas.description:
Captures gentleness deployed as a discipline, not a temperament. Fred Rogers turns out to have been exactly as radical as he appeared: using children's television to insist, slowly and on purpose, that every child is lovable as they are.

An exploration of the life, lessons, and legacy of iconic children's television host Fred Rogers.

metas.name: Diego Maradona
metas.description:
Captures fame as a hostage situation where the hostage keeps scoring goals. Kapadia builds Maradona's Naples years entirely from archive: adored as a god, pulled into the Camorra's orbit, collapsing under a worship no person could survive.

Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the career of celebrated football player Diego Maradona, who played for S.S.C. Napoli in the 1980s.

metas.name: Sherman's March
metas.description:
Captures the personal documentary being invented out of failure. McElwee sets out to film Sherman's Civil War campaign, gets dumped before shooting starts, and the film becomes his disastrous search for love among old flames, narrated in a deadpan spiral.

Documentary filmmaker Ross McElwee sets out to make a movie about Union General Sherman's March to the Sea towards the end of the American Civil War, but keeps getting sidetracked by his own love life.

metas.name: Tarnation
metas.description:
Captures self-documentation as survival strategy. Caouette assembles his life from family photos, answering-machine tapes and home video — a mother destroyed by shock treatments and lithium, a childhood spent performing for cameras — edited on iMovie for a few hundred dollars.

Filmmaker Jonathan Caouette's documentary on growing up with his schizophrenic mother -- a mixture of snapshots, Super-8 film, answering machine messages, video diaries, early short films, and more - culled from nineteen years of ...

metas.name: Best Boy
metas.description:
Captures love expressed as letting go, at the lowest possible volume. Philly, a developmentally disabled man in his fifties whose elderly parents have done everything for him, is gently taught to live more independently — because they won't always be there.

In this documentary, the director follows the day-to-day activities of his intellectually disabled, middle-aged cousin Philly over a three-year period.

metas.name: Andrei Rublev
metas.description:
Captures an artist trying to make images of faith in a world of mud and violence. Medieval Russia through its greatest icon painter: raids, pagan festivals, and a boy casting a bell he may not know how to cast.

The life, times and afflictions of the fifteenth-century Russian iconographer St. Andrei Rublev.

metas.name: Pirosmani
metas.description:
Captures a film learning to see the way its subject painted. Georgian folk painter Niko Pirosmani's life built from his own canvases — taverns, feasts, animals, a man painting signs for food and dying unrecognised.

A biography of the Georgian primitive artist Nikoloz Pirosmanishvili (1862–1918), better known as Pirosmani, who died of starvation and sold his paintings to bars and restaurants for food and drink. The film experiments with color control techniques based on the painter’s style.

metas.name: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
metas.description:
Captures conquest as a fever that keeps marching after its purpose has rotted. Herzog takes a conquistador expedition down the Amazon until the jungle, the raft and Klaus Kinski's face are all dissolving at the same rate.

In the 16th century, the ruthless and insane Don Lope de Aguirre leads a Spanish expedition in search of El Dorado.

metas.name: Caravaggio
metas.description:
Captures a film thinking in paintings the way The Colour of Pomegranates does, but grubbier, queerer, and made for almost no money. Jarman stages the painter's life as living versions of his canvases, with calculators and motorbikes left sitting in the 1600s.

A retelling of the life of the celebrated 17th-century painter through his brilliant, nearly blasphemous paintings and his flirtations with the underworld.

metas.name: 56 Up
metas.description:
Captures time as the special effect. The same British children filmed every seven years from 1964, now 56: the class predictions of the first episode meeting five decades of actual lives. You can feel the series itself ageing.

Director Michael Apted revisits the same group of British-born adults after a seven-year wait. The subjects are interviewed as to the changes that have occurred in their lives during the last seven years.

metas.name: Snowtown
metas.description:
Captures radicalisation as a domestic process. In Adelaide's poorest suburbs, a charismatic man absorbs a vulnerable teenager into his "clean-up" campaign; true story, almost no on-screen violence, dread in every kitchen scene.

Based on true events, 16-year-old Jamie falls in with his mother's new boyfriend and his crowd of self-appointed neighborhood watchmen, a relationship that leads to a spree of torture and murder.

metas.name: The Quince Tree Sun
metas.description:
Captures a painter racing light he knows he'll lose. Antonio López sets up his easel before a quince tree each autumn day, marking the fruit's fall with threads and plumb lines while the radio murmurs the world; a film about trying to fix an observable that changes by the hour. Process cinema at its most patient.

The artist Antonio López tries to capture the sunlight hitting his quince tree all autumn, but the struggle seems futile.

metas.name: Moneyball
metas.description:
Captures competence itself as drama: a general manager and a Yale economist re-deriving baseball from its statistics while the entire sport's intuition laughs at them. The closest film on this list to your actual profession — observed numbers versus inherited scouting folklore, and the numbers are the love story.

Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane's successful attempt to assemble a baseball team on a lean budget by employing computer-generated analysis to acquire new players.
